# 50.44 The Scope of This Stage

What remains later remains later because it is a different question, not because the present verdict is held in suspense.

The present chapter has established why apostolic testimony authenticates the New Testament witness and how that witness stands to earlier Scripture. That establishment is complete for its assignment. What it has not established is the body of writings recognized as Scripture as a dedicated investigation; the canon as the question of which writings constitute the authoritative corpus; prophetic and apostolic authority as canonical recognition; the unity of the written testimony as Movement VII's later file; the distinguishing of revelation, inspiration, and canon as that movement's later file; what inspiration guarantees; why Scripture is an infallible record; John 10:34–36 and “the scripture cannot be broken” as finished Graphē-doctrine; John 17:17 as finished Graphē-doctrine; the Graphē as primary written authority; mishandling, tergiversation, and ἄπειρος (*apeiros*, G552); the scholarly labour of the Graphē, including σπουδάζω (*spoudazō*, G4704); and readiness for the Six First Principles.

Those questions remain later because they are different questions. The present conclusion is already in force for its level.

This chapter has not constructed a canon list. It has not examined prophetic and apostolic authority as canonical recognition. It has not pronounced infallibility as a finished verdict. It has not claimed that the Graphē is primary written authority in the Movement VIII sense. It has not treated John 10:34–36 as finished. It has not treated John 17:17 as finished Graphē-doctrine; it has used John 17's given men and “through their word,” and left “thy word is truth” in its place. It has not entered the First Principles. It has used 2 Peter 1:16–21 as continuity of heed with the prophetic word, and left inspiration's guarantees as already examined in Chapter 30 as a mode of giving, not as this file's substitute, and as due again when Movement VII asks what inspiration guarantees. It has used 2 Peter 3:15–16 as relationship of standing, not as a table of contents.

It has established that apostolic testimony authenticates the New Testament witness as the confirming, positioned, hinge-preaching testimony of those He sent, and that this witness is continuous with the Scriptures He confirmed — fulfillment and handing-on, not replacement and not later rival invention — and that this is Movement VI's closing verdict at this stage.

# 50.45 Apply the Standard

The master formula required definitions, distinctions, premises, biblical record, evidence, competing claims, reasoning, explicit versus inferred, a warranted conclusion, and the next question. Those operations have been performed.

The four governing questions remain distinct.

**Ontological:** What is the case is that this historical Person sent positioned witnesses of His death and raising, whose confirming testimony is the New Testament witness, and that this witness stands to earlier Scripture as fulfillment rather than as replacement. The authority is His-commissioned confirmation, not a later mood about Him.

**Epistemological:** That authority is known through authentic written testimony already warranted, now examined in the specified scenes of preaching, delivery, writing, and location according to the Scriptures, not through an institutional certificate and not through a private impression.

**Evidential:** The warrant is the exhibited bearing of those scenes, under the earned premises of Chapters 27 and 43–49, upon the proposition that apostolic testimony authenticates the New Testament witness and is continuous with earlier Scripture. The reductions fail as global accounts. The closing verdict follows with full force at this level.

**Hermeneutical:** How an authoritative text is later to be handled remains Movements IX–X. This chapter has recorded that the apostles reason out of the Scriptures and that the Bereans search whether those things were so. It has not performed the later discipline of rightly dividing.

The Easton test has been honoured in the relevant sense: the object — the authority of the apostolic testimony as authenticating force for the New Testament witness and as relationship to earlier Scripture — was defined before it was characterised; the biblical scenes were examined rather than replaced by a commentator's summary; the conclusion does not exceed the confirmation and continuity the scenes exhibit.

God has not been reduced to a subject in a book. The Truth who cannot lie, already identified as this Person, is the One who spoke, who sent, whose raising is the hinge, whose Scriptures are fulfilled in Him, and whose hearers confirm the salvation to those who were not there. The later why of the corpus as recognized Scripture, of canon, of guarantees, and of the Graphē as primary written authority remains later. The present honour is already due: the revealer's sent witnesses authenticate the New Testament witness as their confirming testimony, continuous with the writings He confirmed.

The governing maxim remains:

> **Do not make the reader choose between reason and Scripture. Teach the reader to reason through Scripture.**

Reasoning through the writings at this stage, concerning the Person already located, identified, authenticated, examined at the hinge, attested, shown to confirm the writings, and shown to send, yields the authority of the apostolic testimony as Movement VI's closing verdict. That is not the abandonment of historical method. It is the refusal to separate what the record joins, and the refusal to call that joining a postponement.

# 50.46 From Apostolic Testimony to the Scriptural Corpus

The next necessary question is not a new curiosity. It is the question created by the verdict now in force.

He has confirmed the writings. He has appointed witnesses. Their testimony concerning Him is His-commissioned. That testimony authenticates the New Testament witness as their confirming, Scripture-located, written and preached gospel, continuous with earlier Scripture rather than a rival corpus invented later. The writings that present that verdict do not leave unused the further question of the body of writings recognized as Scripture, and of the relationship between earlier and later written witnesses as a dedicated investigation of the corpus.

Authentication of the New Testament witness as apostolic testimony is not yet identification of the scriptural corpus. Continuity with earlier Scripture is not yet the examination of how earlier and later written witnesses constitute one recognized body. 2 Peter 3:15–16 has classed Paul's letters with the other Scriptures as relationship of standing. The classing forces the next file: what, then, is the body of writings so recognized, and how do earlier and later witnesses stand within it?

The question is therefore:

> **What is the scriptural corpus — the body of writings recognized as Scripture — and what is the relationship between earlier and later written witnesses, now that apostolic testimony has been shown to authenticate the New Testament witness as continuous with the Scriptures already confirmed?**

If the authenticating verdict stood as the last word, the book would end with a confirming witness and without the corpus the witness inhabits. If the corpus were identified without the authenticating verdict, Movement VII would have a body of writings without Movement VI's reason for treating the later witnesses as apostolic testimony rather than as a rival library. The remaining file is the remaining file: the scriptural corpus.

That question is not a retreat from apostolic authority. It is apostolic authority examined in the writings as a body. The investigation therefore moves from:

> **Apostolic testimony authenticates the New Testament witness, continuous with earlier Scripture.**

to:

> **What is the body of writings recognized as Scripture, and how do earlier and later written witnesses stand related within it?**

That is the proper open of the next chapter, and of Movement VII. The authority of the apostolic testimony was never meant to be the last word of the book. It was meant to be the last word of Movement VI, sufficient to justify taking the next movement, which is the word the confirming witness itself forces once the sent have preached and written, and once that preaching and writing have been located beside the other Scriptures.

# Chapter Summary

> **The chapter's central conclusion:** Apostolic testimony authenticates the New Testament witness because it is the Lord's sending of positioned witnesses of the death-and-resurrection hinge, confirming to later hearers what He spoke. That authority is not institutional seniority. The same witness does not replace the Scriptures Christ confirmed; it testifies to their fulfillment in Him and hands on what was written of Him. Hebrews 2:3–4 states the chain. Acts preaching makes it public. 1 Corinthians 15:1–11 hands it on as received gospel according to the Scriptures. Luke 1:1–4, John 20:30–31, and John 21:24 deposit it in writing toward certainty and belief. 2 Peter joins eyewitness to prophecy and Paul's letters to the other Scriptures. A rival corpus invented later fails. Canon, guarantees, infallibility, and the Graphē-gate remain later because they are later questions. The closing verdict of Movement VI is in force. The investigation now turns to the scriptural corpus.

The essential architecture is:

> **Sending-relation already in force → authenticating force for the New Testament witness as the next object → authority defined as confirmation, not seniority → distinctions that protect the object → threefold ground → Hebrews 2:3–4 → Acts preaching → received gospel → written deposition → continuity with earlier Scripture → failure of reductions → closing verdict warranted → sequence to Movement VII.**

The governing distinctions are:

- **Existence, identity, claims-and-works, hinge, seers, confirmation of Scripture, and sending-relation** are Chapters 43–49; **the authority of the apostolic testimony** is this chapter's object.
- **Institutional seniority** is not **this authenticating force**.
- **Replacement of earlier Scripture** is not **fulfillment-testimony**.
- **Authentication of the New Testament witness** is not **canon-list construction**.
- **Relationship of standing** is not **the closed corpus**.
- **This verdict** is not **inspiration's guarantees, infallibility, or the Graphē-gate**.
- **Scope** is sequence of levels, not hesitation about this level.

The decisive principle is:

> **Examine why the commissioned, positioned, hinge-preaching testimony of those He sent authenticates the New Testament witness, and how that witness stands to the Scriptures already confirmed, before identifying the scriptural corpus, constructing the canon, or drawing the Graphē-gate. Draw the conclusion the premises support. Do not draw the conclusions that still require later premises. Then ask what the body of writings recognized as Scripture is, and how earlier and later written witnesses stand related within it.**
